mechanism_claims.claim_text: S5 and S7 are supported by direct source assays as membrane-active peptides: LPS/LTA binding, membrane depolarization, beta-galactosidase release, microscopy-localized membrane damage, and ROS increase are all described for E. coli and/or S. aureus models.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Table 2 supports pathogen-selective MIC activity for the S1-S7 panel, with S5 and S7 among the strongest pathogen-active peptides and probiotic Lactobacillus rows largely >64 µM.
mechanism_claims.limitations: This is a phenotypic selectivity claim, not a direct molecular mechanism.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Table 3 supports salt/serum susceptibility behavior for S5 and S7 against E. coli ATCC 25922 and S. aureus ATCC 29213 under defined salt and serum conditions.
